text:
Marathon Petroleum is up 0.7% today as crude oil prices remain elevated and U.S. refineries are running at near-capacity (96.8%). The stock has climbed 9.6% over two weeks as oil has stayed above $107 per barrel—higher prices generally benefit refiners, who profit from the difference between what they pay for crude and what they sell refined products for. Today's move fits a steady uptrend since mid-September as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East (Saudi pipeline concerns, Pakistan-Iran energy disputes, and broader conflict escalation) have kept global oil prices firm at $130.80 per barrel.

The refining sector is also seeing tailwinds from tight inventory levels: gasoline and diesel stockpiles are relatively lean, which typically supports margins for refiners. Record diesel prices mentioned in recent reports signal strong demand and pricing power across fuel products, which feeds directly into refiner profitability.
